newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN STRETCH LEAD AFTER 3-0 WIN AT HAMBURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN STRETCH LEAD AFTER 3-0 WIN AT HAMBURG.

text.p: Bayern Munich cast aside their internal problems with a 3-0 victory at Hamburg on Saturday to stretch their lead at the top of the German first division to three points.
Goals from striker Juergen Klinsmann and midfielder Mario Basler, who have both been at the centre of controversy after being substituted last weekend, put the Bavarians 2-0 up at halftime.
A second-half strike from German international defender Thomas Helmer helped Bayern take a three-point lead over second-placed Borussia Dortmund.
Reigning champions Dortmund warmed up for their European Cup semifinal against England's Manchester United on Wednesday with a 2-0 home win over highly-placed Bochum.
Swiss striker Stephane Chapuisat scored in the 33rd and 72nd minutes, the second from a penalty.

But the champions finished the match with 10 men after libero Matthias Sammer was sent off late in the second half for his second bookable offence. The German international is also suspended for the European Cup first leg in Dortmund.
Dortmund moved up to second place, replacing Bayer Leverkusen who lost ground in the tight title race after a surprise 1-0 defeat at relegation-threatened Hansa Rostock.
Leverkusen are now five points behind the leaders. Fourth-placed VfB Stuttgart have a chance to leap over them when they visit bottom club Freiburg on Sunday.

Basler upset his Bayern team mates by leaving the ground before the final whistle last weekend. Klinsmann was reported to have left shortly afterwards. Captain Lothar Matthaeus said they had not shown team spirit.
